VERDICT: EXTEND C0004 | `scan_health()` marks a tool available whenever its runner returns without raising, but `_run_tool()` encodes both `NOT_FOUND` and `TIMEOUT` as normal `CompletedProcess(returncode=-1, stderr=...)`. This means tool availability is overstated not only for missing binaries but also for timed-out tools. Downstream, `HealthScan.tools_available` can report a sick tool as healthy, misleading the insect brain’s health signal and any operator reading the report. The existing fix should treat timeout/nonzero launcher failure as unavailable at the source of truth, not just parse missing binaries.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually sandbox tests against the patched source tree. In `bench/endocrine.py`, it writes only the patched target file into a tempdir as `tmpdir/<basename>` and then runs `test_cmd` with `cwd=tmpdir`, but it never copies the rest of the project, rewrites path arguments, or puts the patched file back into its package-relative location. Any command like the immune pipeline’s `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]` will run from a tempdir that does not contain `bench/tests/` or the package under test, so tests either fail for environmental reasons or execute against the original source outside the sandbox. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`; no `shutil.copytree`, no package layout recreation, no command rewriting; later `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`.
FOLLOW: This breaks the key claimed capability “sandbox-test proposed fixes.” Downstream, fix verdicts become misleading in both directions: valid fixes can be marked HARMFUL because pytest cannot find the test tree from `tmpdir`, and test commands that reference installed/original code can pass without exercising the patched file, falsely marking a fix SAFE. The immune pipeline depends on `evaluate_fixes()` to set `finding.verified=True`; if verification is detached from the patched sandbox, the bug-closed gate in `immune_agents.py` can close findings on evidence that never actually tested the candidate fix against the modified code. That is a HIGH/near-CRITICAL interface failure because it silently corrupts reviewer-facing verdicts.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — create a sandbox copy of the relevant project tree, not just the single file: copy the repository subtree containing `source_paths` and tests into `tmpdir`, write the patched file back to its original relative path inside that copy, then run `test_cmd` inside that sandbox so imports and test paths resolve against patched code only.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as SAFE even when it introduces new issues, because it sums net deltas across different tools and treats only positive total as harmful. Example: `net_type_errors = +3`, `net_ruff_errors = -5`, `net_bandit_issues = 0` gives `total_net = -2`, so verdict becomes SAFE despite three new type errors. Evidence: `total_net = result.net_type_errors + result.net_ruff_errors + result.net_bandit_issues`; `if total_net > 0: HARMFUL`, `if total_net < 0: SAFE`.
FOLLOW: This directly corrupts fix evaluation, the endocrine layer’s highest-consequence feature. A fix that regresses one dimension while improving another can be marked SAFE and then propagated to the immune pipeline as programmatically verified. Downstream, `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` marks findings `verified=True` for SAFE or NEUTRAL results, enabling duplicate closure and preventing further scrutiny of a still-broken bug. This is silently wrong output, not merely a threshold preference.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive per-tool delta as HARMFUL before considering aggregate improvement: if `net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`, return HARMFUL; otherwise keep the existing SAFE/NEUTRAL logic for all-nonpositive deltas.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` measures pre-fix diagnostics on the original file path but post-fix diagnostics on an isolated temp file with a different path and no surrounding package context. For tools like pyright and mypy, diagnostics depend on module location, imports, and package-relative resolution; comparing counts from `target_path` versus `tmpdir/<basename>` is not like-for-like. Evidence: pre counts call runners on `target_path`; post counts call runners on `patched_path` in a temp dir containing only one file.
FOLLOW: Even if tests are omitted, the static-analysis delta used for SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL is unreliable. Import-related errors can disappear or appear solely because the file was moved out of its package, not because the fix changed semantics. Downstream, the endocrine report can claim a fix reduced or introduced type issues when the count change is an artifact of path relocation. That feeds the same verification/closure path in the immune pipeline and misleads human reviewers about whether the patch is safe.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — run both pre- and post-fix tool checks in the same sandboxed project layout, using the same relative file path for the target file before and after patching, so only the code change varies.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.33
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `scan_health()` omits unavailable tools from `tools_available` entirely when `source_paths` is empty or when a runner returns `[]` on launcher failure, producing an ambiguous report shape. The report consumer cannot distinguish “tool absent”, “tool present and found zero diagnostics”, and “no scan run.” Evidence: empty-input path returns `HealthScan(elapsed_s=...)` with default empty `tools_available`; normal path only sets keys inside the loop and relies on runner success rather than actual execution status.
FOLLOW: The insect brain receives an under-specified health report. Missing keys force consumers to infer state from absence, while other cases use explicit booleans. This weakens interface correctness and compounds C0001/C0004: the endocrine layer can both overstate health and omit state entirely depending on path. Downstream dashboards or logic comparing tool readiness across rounds can misread disappearing keys as schema drift or healthy zero-findings scans.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — always populate `tools_available` for every configured tool with explicit booleans, including the no-source-path early return, and derive those booleans from actual tool execution status rather than empty diagnostic lists.
VERIFIED: TRUE
